title: Deep learning brain age from routine CT is linked to stroke outcome
summary: In 1,173 acute ischemic stroke patients from a prospective multicenter cohort, a deep learning model estimated brain age from contralesional baseline non-contrast CT. Brain age gap was higher in patients than in controls (+3.1 +/- 9.1 years) and higher gap was associated with worse 90-day functional status after adjustment (proportional odds ratio 1.091 per 5 years; 95% CI 1.023 to 1.162; p=0.008). It added only modest discrimination, and the authors call for external validation.
ai_technology: Deep learning brain-age estimation from contralesional non-contrast CT

evidence.tested: Association with 90-day functional outcome in a prospective multicenter cohort (n=1,173), adjusted for age, sex, severity and treatment.
evidence.unknown: No external validation; clinical decision value untested; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep learning model estimated brain age, used as a marker of brain vulnerability.
